Across HubPool custody and Aave Portal settlement
Research date: 29 September 2026. This is a read-only assessment of the proposed flow “purchased
pDAI → Across HubPool → Aave → backUnbacked.” It distinguishes the deployed interfaces and their
accounting from a separately authorized integration that might connect them.
Finding
The copied HubPool's standard liquidity operations do not automatically lend DAI into Aave or settle an
Aave Portal obligation. addLiquidity takes actual DAI into HubPool and issues an Across LP claim. 
backUnbacked takes actual DAI into Aave and reduces its previously issued unbacked balance. These are
distinct cash movements with different outstanding claims.
A separately integrated arrangement could connect the systems, but its cash movement and treatment
of Across LP claims would need to be specified. The observed HubPool includes governed adapter calls,
so absence of an Aave-named entry point is not proof that every possible custom integration is
impossible. It is evidence that the proposed lending step is not supplied automatically by the standard
operations reviewed here.
Source and observation boundary
HubPool is 0xc186fa914353c44b2e33ebe05f21846f1048beda. Its explorer-verified deployed source and ABI were
reviewed alongside the May 2023 repository source. The versions have some source differences,
including the default identifier; the relevant liquidity, reserve-sync and adapter accounting operations
support the conclusions below. Repository availability is not substituted for deployed behavior where the
verified source is available.
Endpoint reads use PulseChain block 27,659,393, hash 
0xc5e582cd902f4bff3b1aa325b9b564fcd5d6dc0ffa77a03fcd105b65c6390275. Actual cash and recorded reserve results
are preserved in the companion batch artifacts/parb-across-accounting-20260929/reserve_reads.json.

In deployed HubPool addLiquidity, exchange-rate synchronization occurs before the new deposit, then the
contract issues LP shares and receives the underlying. In removeLiquidity, the LP claim is burned and the
actual underlying is paid out; available liquid reserves and token cash constrain that payment.
An unsolicited transfer is different. _sync treats excess underlying balance as cash returning to the pool: it
raises liquid reserves and decreases utilized reserves. Ignoring fees and other concurrent changes, their
sum does not increase from this reclassification alone. A direct transfer therefore cannot be treated
simultaneously as a newly issued Across LP position, a new independent receivable, and a completed
Aave settlement.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 93

Aave supply is not Portal backing
The historical Aave Pool interface and BridgeLogic separate ordinary supply from settlement of
previously issued unbacked aT okens. backUnbacked uses the lesser of the requested amount and
outstanding unbacked principal, reduces that outstanding balance, and transfers underlying plus any
specified fee into the aT oken contract. It is restricted through Aave's bridge authorization. It does not
mint an additional aT oken principal position for the party paying the backing.
Consequently, lending 100 DAI to Aave through ordinary supply can create a 100-DAI-denominated
aT oken position, but it does not also discharge a separate 100-DAI Portal obligation. Paying 100 DAI
through backUnbacked can discharge that obligation, but it does not simultaneously give its payer another
fresh 100-DAI aT oken claim. The same distinction applies when the funding originated from a purchase,
an Across LP redemption, or some other transfer.
If Across LP claims remain outstanding while their supporting cash is committed to settle someone else's
already-issued aT oken liability, the Across balance sheet needs a corresponding real asset or an explicit
extinguishment of its claim. Merely labelling the movement “lending” does not establish either. An
Across LP token is not automatically an aT oken, and an Aave balance is not automatically included in
HubPool's ordinary reserve calculation.

The two nonzero adapter addresses match the pinned historical deployment records for 
Ethereum_Adapter and Arbitrum_Adapter. These are stored keys in copied state; the key 1 does not itself
change the execution chain back to Ethereum or prove a live remote connection.
The historical Ethereum adapter is a same-chain pass-through: its token operation transfers tokens to
the designated recipient, and its message operation calls its designated target. The Arbitrum adapter
uses the canonical bridge/router and messaging interfaces. These source paths do not define a native
Aave lending strategy or automatically invoke Portal settlement. This is an assessment of the identified
historical adapters, not every possible adapter contract.
HubPool executes adapter code through delegatecall in the HubPool context. Standard positive pool-
rebalance sends reduce liquid reserves and increase utilized reserves as assets are sent toward the
configured spoke. The base exchange-rate calculation uses liquid reserves, utilized reserves and
undistributed LP fees; it does not independently discover or value arbitrary Aave investments. Governed
adapter composition is therefore a meaningful extension point, but its existence is not evidence that the
hypothesized HubPool-to-Aave investment and claim reconciliation already occurred.
The HubPool ABI contains neither an Aave supply/deposit method nor a Portal backUnbacked method. Its 
multicall batches supported HubPool operations; that name is not evidence of a general Aave lending
service. No actual HubPool→Aave lending or Portal-settlement transaction was identified in this bounded
source/accounting review. It was not an exhaustive search of every HubPool transaction or every
separately configured adapter.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 94

Configured SpokePool: historical callback and a later implementation change
The configured key-1 SpokePool is 0x5c7bcd6e7de5423a257d81b442095a1a6ced35c5. It must not be confused with
the older 0x4d9079bb4165aeb4084c526a32695dcfd2f77381 deployment inspected elsewhere. The older address's
ABI does not establish this configured proxy's callback capabilities.
At inherited block 17,232,999, the configured proxy's implementation is 
0xa667498f46457548f1d3ad557340b95fdb290148. Its verified Ethereum_SpokePool implementation and included
SpokePool source do contain destination message callbacks. The deposit and fill interfaces include
message bytes. Following token payout, a contract recipient with a nonempty message can receive 
handleAcrossMessage with the token, amount, whether the fill is complete, the relayer and the message. The
self-relay branch returns earlier without the transfer or callback.
This corrects any broader conclusion that the configured copied SpokePool lacked callbacks at the fork.
The historical callback supports conditional destination composition with a compatible recipient. It does
not make Aave's Pool itself an Across message handler or establish that an actual recipient already
supplies assets to Aave or performs authorized Portal settlement. The verified inherited ABI has no Aave-
specific lending/backing entry point.
At the endpoint the proxy instead points to 0x788e49c4e2b3414777d6671d7411951e81d35808. Transaction 0x4c07…
7ee4 successfully upgraded it at block 26,912,634, 30 June 2026, 04:52:25 UTC, block hash 
0xc8f90908ec94d2608cb6e88eeabc9538f21767014f38b2abe7187b916131b859. The sender was HubPool's observed owner
0xfeca7291cebe75789ffa707754db259187b1d140. The actual trace runs through HubPool, its Ethereum adapter
and the configured SpokePool's upgrade operation. It uses stored chain key 1 on PulseChain.
The old implementation has 22,759 bytes of runtime code at the inherited block; the endpoint
implementation has 2,191 bytes of runtime code at the endpoint. The explorer returns no verified
source or ABI for the new implementation. Code size alone does not identify its functionality. This study
therefore does not claim that the current implementation retains the inherited callback, removes it, or
adds Aave methods. The historical capability and the later unverified implementation are separate
findings.
Likewise, the zero mapping under key 369 is an observation about one stored configuration key, not
proof that every possible Across operation stops on PulseChain. The successful key-1 administrative
trace demonstrates that at least that configured same-chain message path operated there. Whether a
particular source/destination liquidity route is consistent with the deployed chain-ID rules requires that
route's own evidence; changing the label does not by itself create liquidity or an Aave integration.
The new observations are preserved separately under artifacts/parb-mapped-spoke-20260929/: inherited/
endpoint implementation and code reads, the proxy upgrade log, successful receipt and trace, block
metadata, and both explorer source responses. All were read-only.
Implication for the proposed loop
Buying existing pDAI and moving it into HubPool can replenish Across cash. Moving that pDAI into Aave
can instead fund an Aave supply position or settle Portal, according to the actual method and
authorization used. A complete ledger must identify which claim is created, retained or discharged at
each movement. No individual unit can remain spendable HubPool cash and also be cash already
delivered to Aave at the same instant.
The missing link in the standard-interface description is an observed or explicitly stipulated integration
that moves the assets and reconciles those claims. This is compatible with conditional architectural
analysis; it is not filled simply by assuming that an Across deposit is automatically lent into Aave or that
ordinary Aave supply equals backUnbacked.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 95

New source and adapter-read evidence is preserved under ignored artifacts/parb-hub-aave-
accounting-20260929/. Public access was read-only. No simulated transactions, privileged calls or
configuration changes were performed.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 96
